title: PLA ADIZ Incursion Spikes to 14 Sorties, 11 Crossing Median Line — Largest Since Mid-July
detail: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense tracked 14 PLA aircraft sorties, 6 PLAN vessels and 8 official ships operating around Taiwan in the 24-hour window ending 06:00 (UTC+8) on August 8, 2026. Of the 14 sorties, 11 crossed the Taiwan Strait median line and entered Taiwan's northern and southwestern ADIZ sectors — the largest single-day sortie count since the July 30 spike (12 sorties, 10 crossing) and occurring on day three of Taiwan's Han Kuang 42 live-fire exercise (Aug 5-14). Taiwan deployed combat air patrol aircraft, naval vessels and coastal missile systems in response.

title: Lai Boards Missile Boat as Han Kuang Coastal Drill Tests New Strike Drones
detail: President Lai Ching-te boarded a Kuang Hua VI-class missile boat at Tsoying Naval Base in Kaohsiung on August 8, 2026, to inspect a coastal-defense exercise simulating repulsion of a Chinese amphibious/warship incursion — part of day four of the Han Kuang 42 live-fire exercise. The drill integrated the newly stood-up Littoral Combat Command: a 750-ton Anping-class patrol vessel (Bali, CG-606) led four Kuang Hua VI missile boats armed with Hsiung Feng II anti-ship missiles, alongside special-operations craft. Troops also tested two prototype attack-drone types supplied by the Armaments Bureau — medium-class kamikaze/loitering drones that hovered near the beach before simulating strikes on designated targets. Lai called on personnel to 'respond proactively to a range of scenarios and strengthen their combat readiness.'
